findings.excerpt:
calc
      _ = unitIso.inv ≫ (restriction.map s ≫ restriction.map g.hom) ≫ f.hom :=
        (Category.assoc _ _ _).trans
          (congrArg (fun morphism => unitIso.inv ≫ morphism)
            (Category.assoc _ _ _).symm)
      _ = unitIso.inv ≫ restriction.map (s ≫ g.hom) ≫ f.hom :=
        congrArg (fun morphism => unitIso.inv ≫ morphism ≫ f.hom)
          (restriction.map_comp s g.hom).symm
      _ = _ := (Category.assoc _ _ _).symm
findings.problem: The calculation manually transports equalities through compositions and repeatedly reassociates them, although the intermediate claim is simply preservation of composition by the restriction functor.
findings.proposed_change:
Keep the statement of `composition`, but replace its entire `calc` proof with:
```lean
    simp only [Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc]
```
findings.benefit: The explicit lemma list exposes exactly the same mathematical idea—functoriality and associativity—without requiring readers to track nested congruence and transitivity steps. No hypotheses change; the argument also applies to an empty affine open.

evidence.excerpt:
/-- A functor preserves composition. -/
  map_comp : ∀ {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z), map (f ≫ g) = map f ≫ map g := by cat_disch

/-- Composition in a category is associative. -/
  assoc : ∀ {W X Y Z : obj} (f : W ⟶ X) (g : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z), (f ≫ g) ≫ h = f ≫ g ≫ h := by
    cat_disch
